sentences.text:
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.27676 Of 2008
ORDER:
Heard learned Counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of respondents and perused the record.

2. Shorn of unnecessary details, the case of the petitioner in brief, is that the 2nd respondent had passed Award in respect of petitioner's land, vide Award dated 27.03.2006 under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act'); that since there is a dispute with regard to apportionment,
the 2nd respondent authority had referred the dispute to the decision of the Court as per Section 30 of the Act; and that the 2nd respondent by proceedings dated 10.11.2008 had rejected the application made by the petitioner on 03.11.2008 under Section 18 of the Act, without awaiting the result of the decision of the Court with regard to the apportionment of compensation as awarded,
vide Award dated 27.03.2006.
3.

Petitioner further contends that on the 2nd respondent making reference of the dispute to the Court an order was passed on 04.09.2008 and it is only on passing of the said order, the right of the petitioner to claim compensation has been crystalised and, as such, the petitioner is entitled to file application under Section 18 of the Act with regard to quantum of compensation awarded thereafter.

4. Petitioner further contends that the memo by which the 2nd respondent authority had rejected the application of the petitioner on the ground that the said application is filed after one year of passing of Award is illegal, arbitrary and contrary to the provisions of the Act.

In support of the aforesaid contentions, reliance is placed on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Madan v. State of Maharashtra 1.
5.

Per contra, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of respondents submits that since the Award has been passed on 27.03.2006, an application under Section 18 of the Act is required to be preferred within six weeks or two months from the date of service of notice by the Collector under Section 12 of sub-section 2 of the Act as applicable in the State of A.P. (then);
and that as the petitioner had made the application under Section 18 of the Act on 1 (2014) 2 SCC 720 03.11.2008, the same is beyond the period of time prescribed under the Act and as such the 2nd respondent has issued the memo dated 10.11.2008 rejecting the application submitted by the petitioner.

sentences.text: I have taken note of the respective contentions urged.

7. A similar issue as that of the issue involved in the present Writ Petition has fallen for consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Madan (case supra) whereby their Lordships while considering the scope of provisions of Sections 18 and 30 of the Act have held as under:
"A cursory glance at the provisions of Sections 18 and 30 of the Act, extracted above,
may suggest that there is some overlapping between the provisions inasmuch as both contemplate reference of the issue of apportionment of compensation to the court.
But, a closer scrutiny would indicate that the two sections of the Act operate in entirely different circumstances.

While Section 18 applies to situations where the apportionment made in the award is objected to by a beneficiary thereunder, Section 30 applies when no apportionment whatsoever is made by the Collector on account of conflicting claims.
In such a situation one of the options open to the Collector is to make a reference of the question of apportionment to the court under Section 30 of the Act.
The other is to relegate the parties to the remedy of a suit.

In either situation,
the right to receive compensation under the award would crystallise after apportionment is made in favour of a claimant.

It is only thereafter that a reference under Section 18 for enhanced compensation can be legitimately sought by the claimant in whose favour the order of apportionment is passed either by the court in the reference under Section 30 or in the civil suit, as may be."
8.

Since, in the facts of the present case, the 2nd respondent authority having taken note of the fact of existence of a dispute and having made a reference to the Court under Section 30 of the Act could not have rejected the application made by the petitioner observing the same as having been filed beyond the period of 60 days prescribed under the Act.

The entitlement of the petitioner to receive the compensation under the Award has, in fact, been crystalised only on 03.09.2008 when the competent Court of civil jurisdiction by its above order in O.P. No.115 of 2007 had determined the petitioner's entitlement.
It is only thereafter the petitioner had filed application under Section 18 of the Act on 03.11.2008 which is well within the 60 days time period as provided under the Act.

9. In view of the above, this Court is of the view that the impugned proceeding/memo dated 10.11.2008 as issued by the 2nd respondent rejecting the application filed by the petitioner under Section 18 of the Act cannot be sustained.

10. Accordingly, the impugned proceeding is set aside and the 2nd respondent authority is directed to make a reference of the application made by the petitioner under Section 18 of the Act on 03.11.2008 to the civil Court within six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of the order as provided under the Act for proper adjudication and determination of compensation payable.
11. Subject to the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
